source.title: A Theoretical-Empirical Approach to Estimating Sample Complexity of DNNs
source.authors: Devansh Bisla; Apoorva Nandini Saridena; A. Choromańska

record.file_problem: none noted; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: Reports empirical learning curves for natural-label classification as training-set size changes and measurements of effective feature dimensionality. This bears conceptually on natural-label generalization and a measured property associated with it, but does not test the claim's random-label memorization comparison or most listed interventions.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-error learning curves for natural-label tasks and effective-dimensionality measurements. It does not train on random labels. Cited results on fitting random labels are prior work and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests a sample-complexity estimator, not any of V1–V8. Natural-label learning curves do not test coexistence with random-label memorization; capacity sweeps measure effective dimensionality rather than test error past interpolation. The original random-label finding is cited as background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but needs its scope stated: the authors conclude that their assumption-based estimator approximates empirical learning curves across tested tasks, particularly in the power-law region. They acknowledge low-data mismatch and incomplete training fit on ImageNet. The radius is fitted using learning-curve observations from training subsets of at most 50%.
record.recipe_differences: Estimates sample-complexity learning curves from an assumed feature-space error model and measured effective dimensionality; trains conventional models on natural labels, without the random-label memorization comparison central to the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effective dimensionality depends indirectly on model capacity; the fitted radius δ differs substantially by dataset and architecture. The authors report mismatch in the low-data overfitting region and better fit in the power-law region.

fits_no_version.finding: Empirical performance improves with training-set size in the power-law region; the estimator mismatches the low-data overfitting region.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A feature-distance model with empirically estimated dimensionality and fitted radius can approximate natural-label learning curves in the tested power-law regimes.

fits_no_version.finding: Bottleneck experiments give low selected effective dimensionalities, although CIFAR-100 and ImageNet bottleneck accuracies remain below their original-model baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuned bottleneck accuracy can saturate at low feature dimensions without fully preserving original-model accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Measured effective dimensionality increases as capacity decreases in the reported MNIST sweeps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effective feature dimensionality depends on network capacity in the tested MNIST architectures.

record.peer_reviewed: 2021 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
record.problems: The generalization-error model assumes zero training error and an assumed feature-distance error mechanism; ImageNet does not satisfy the zero-training-error assumption. The authors report low-data-regime mismatch. Empirical learning curves are primarily shown in figures, and exact curve values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in text. The study is not a test of random-label memorization or the listed intervention comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No additional separately stated numeric learning-curve values are available in the supplied text; figures show curves without tabulated numeric points. Supplementary Table 5 nearest-neighbor feature-vector accuracies were left out because they do not directly measure a claim version or a result proposed under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: No random-label experiment or matched natural-versus-random-label comparison; natural-label accuracy alone does not establish coexistence.
No test-error width sweep with the zero-training-error threshold identified.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected test-error comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
No matched adaptive-optimizer-versus-SGD comparison or tuning-budget comparison.
No within-workload batch-size comparison or recipe adaptation experiment.
No dropout ablation, dropout-strength sweep, or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or ranking against generalization gaps and competing measures.
No memorization-based example removal and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All rows concern findings outside V1–V8, so cannot_determine denotes their inability to establish a specified version, not absence of their reported trends. Bottleneck dimensionalities are estimator-selection quantities; they should not be presented as direct evidence for V2 or V7.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of random-label and natural-label test performance.
No width sweep testing test error beyond the zero-training-error threshold; the MLP width table reports effective dimensionality only.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison to norm- or margin-based measures.

rows.value: Figure 3 and Figure 9 show the empirical learning curve; exact values are not stated in text.

rows.subject: CovNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained on increasing subsets of Udacity; measured test error using a steering-command deviation threshold.

conditions.value: Misclassified if predicted steering command deviates from label by more than 0.1

rows.note: Authors state that performance consistently improves with more training data in the power-law region; the figure's regression error is defined by the stated threshold.
rows.check: Steering prediction versus training-set size measures none of the specified versions. Adam and dropout are used without comparator ablations.
